# Maester Test Expert

Create, edit, validate, and document Maester security checks -- the unit of work that assesses a Microsoft 365
tenant's security posture.

From Maester 3.0 every check is a **native test**: two files, `Test.<ID>.ps1` and `Test.<ID>.md`. There are no
`*.Tests.ps1` wrappers, no separate helper function in `powershell/public/`, no `maester-config.json` row and no
`FunctionsToExport` entry. Maester's own engine discovers the test from its attribute, checks that the services and
licences it declares are available, runs it, catches errors and writes the result row.

The user-facing guide with every rule is `website/docs/writing-tests/index.mdx`. This skill is the contributor's
condensed version; if they disagree, the code and that page win. How to choose the value of each classification,
priority and ATT&CK attribute is in `website/docs/writing-tests/attribute-rubric.md` (the rubric); this skill
links to it and does not repeat it.

## Agent Selection

Use **maester-test-expert** as the primary agent for all normal workflows.

Specialized planner and issue-manager agents are optional workflow components and should generally stay in the
background to avoid user confusion.

## When to Use This Skill

- Creating a new Maester security check
- Editing or refactoring an existing check
- Adding or correcting a check's attributes: product, feature, area, resource type, severity, user impact,
  implementation cost, ATT&CK techniques, service or licence declarations
- Writing or updating a check's `.md` (description, remediation, result template)
- Reviewing a check for correctness, duplication with a test in another suite, attributes that fit the rubric, or
  documentation completeness
- Debugging a failing, erroring or skipped check
- Writing or converting a user's custom test (`custom/` folder)

**Do NOT use this skill for:**

- Editing EIDSCA tests by hand -- `tests/eidsca/Test.EIDSCA.*` are generated by `build/eidsca/Update-EidscaTests.ps1`
  from templates in `build/eidsca/templates/`. Change the generator or its data.
- Editing ORCA tests by hand -- `tests/orca/Test.ORCA.*` (header "Generated by ./build/orca/Update-OrcaTests.ps1")
  and `powershell/internal/generated/orca/check-ORCA*.ps1` are generated. Change the generator.
- Editing `website/docs/tests/` -- test pages are generated from the test files by
  `website/scripts/generate-test-docs.mjs`.
- Unit tests of the module itself (`powershell/tests/`).

## Prerequisites

- PowerShell 7.4 or later.
- A source checkout: `Import-Module ./powershell/Maester.psd1` loads the module and defines every built-in test from
  `./tests`. No build and no .NET SDK are needed unless you change `src/Maester.Engine`.
- A working `Connect-Maester` session to run a check against a tenant.
- Review the Maester [contribution guidelines](../../../website/docs/contributing.md) before submitting changes.

## Anatomy of a Check

| File | Location | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Test.<ID>.ps1` | `tests/<suite>/[<service>/]` | One function with a `[MaesterTest(...)]` attribute. Reads the tenant, decides, calls `Add-MtTestResultDetail`, returns `$true`/`$false`. |
| `Test.<ID>.md` | Same folder, same base name | Description, `#### Remediation action`, optional `#### Related links`, then `<!--- Results --->` and `%TestResult%`. Shown in the report. |
| `suite.json` | Each suite folder (already exists) | The suite's ID, name, `Source` and help URL template. Do not edit for a single check. |
| `frameworks/<key>.json` | Beside the `suite.json` of the CIS, CISA and ASD suites | The catalogue of the benchmark: its name and version, and one entry per requirement with its level, profiles or criticality (ASD: maturity level and strategy, or ISM guideline, section and applicability). It does not list tests. A CIS, CISA or ASD check names its requirement in `Control`; add the requirement here in the same pull request if it is new, or the build fails. The ASD files are generated by `build/asd/Update-AsdFramework.ps1`. |

Suite folders: `tests/maester/<service>/` (`MT.xxxx`; services such as `entra`, `exchange`, `teams`, `defender`,
`azure`, `intune`, and `xspm` for exposure management, which has its own `suite.json`), `tests/cisa/<service>/`
(`CISA.MS.*`), `tests/cis/` (`CIS.M365.*`), `tests/asd/<service>/` (`ASD.ISM-xxxx`, named after the ISM control the
check implements), `tests/ad/<area>/` (`AD-*`), and the generated `tests/eidsca/` and
`tests/orca/`. Every folder name is lowercase kebab-case; see the repository layout in
[the contributing guide](../../../website/docs/contributing.md#repository-layout).

The function keeps a descriptive name (`Test-MtCaMfaForRiskySignIn`). Function names must be unique across
`powershell/internal`, `powershell/public` and every test file, because built-in tests share the module scope.
Code shared by several checks goes in `powershell/internal/checks/<suite>/<service>/` as an internal helper;
reusable data access for a service goes in `powershell/internal/services/<service>/`.

## The Test File

### Template

Scaffold it, then edit:

```powershell
New-MtTest -Id MT.1234 -Title 'At least one Conditional Access policy blocks device code flow.' `
    -Product entra -Feature conditional-access -Area authentication -ResourceType Tenant `
    -Severity High -UserImpact Low -ImplementationCost Low -Mitre T1078.004, T1528, T1566 `
    -Service Graph -Path ./tests/maester/entra
```

Only `-Id` and `-Title` are required, so you can scaffold first and set the other values once the `.md` is
written (see [Choosing the attribute values](#choosing-the-attribute-values)). `New-MtTest` does not write
`Author`; add it.

```powershell
function Test-MtCaBlockDeviceCodeFlow {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Checks if at least one enabled Conditional Access policy blocks the device code flow.

    .DESCRIPTION
    {Detailed description of the control and what the check evaluates.}
    #>
    [MaesterTest(
        Id                 = 'MT.1234',
        Title              = 'At least one Conditional Access policy blocks device code flow.',
        Product            = 'entra',
        Feature            = 'conditional-access',
        Area               = 'authentication',
        ResourceType       = 'Tenant',
        Severity           = 'High',
        UserImpact         = 'Low',
        ImplementationCost = 'Low',
        Mitre              = ('T1078.004', 'T1528', 'T1566'),
        Control            = ('cisa-scuba:MS.AAD.3.1', 'nist-800-53-r5:IA-2'),
        Service            = 'Graph',
        License            = 'AAD_PREMIUM',
        Author             = 'your-github-handle'
    )]
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([bool])]
    param()

    $policies = Get-MtConditionalAccessPolicy | Where-Object { $_.state -eq 'enabled' }
    $blocking = @($policies | Where-Object {
            $_.conditions.authenticationFlows.transferMethods -match 'deviceCodeFlow' -and
            $_.grantControls.builtInControls -contains 'block'
        })

    if ($blocking.Count -gt 0) {
        $result = "Well done. These policies block the device code flow:`n`n%TestResult%"
        Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result $result -GraphObjects $blocking -GraphObjectType ConditionalAccess
        return $true
    }

    Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result 'No enabled Conditional Access policy blocks the device code flow.'
    return $false
}
```

Note what is **not** there: no `Test-MtConnection` guard, no `Get-MtLicenseInformation` check, no outer
`try`/`catch`, no `-Description`, no `-Severity`, no `-TestTitle`, and no `Tag`.

### File rules (enforced by `Read-MtNativeTest`; violations are `InvalidMetadata`)

- File name is exactly `Test.<Id>.ps1`; the `.md` sits beside it.
- Exactly one function with `[MaesterTest(...)]`. Other functions (private helpers, a family's instance source) may
  live in the same file.
- Top level contains only function definitions: no statements, no script `param()` block.
- The test function has `[CmdletBinding()]`.

A benchmark check's ID is the suite prefix, then the requirement's ID as the benchmark writes it, without a
version suffix: `CIS.M365.5.2.2.2`, `CISA.MS.AAD.3.1` (SCuBA `MS.AAD.3.1v1`), `ASD.ISM-1504` (ASD writes
`ISM-1504` with a hyphen). The part after the prefix is the requirement's `Id` in the framework file, which the
unit tests check. See [Test IDs](../../../website/docs/writing-tests/index.mdx#test-ids).

### The `[MaesterTest]` attribute

Arguments are **named and constant**: quoted strings, `$true`/`$false`, a parenthesised list `('a', 'b')`, a single
string for a list property, or a bare flag (`LongRunning`). No variables, expressions, `@()` or hashtables. The
schema lives in `powershell/assets/MaesterTestSchema.psd1`. How to choose the values from `Product` to `Mitre` is
in [Choosing the attribute values](#choosing-the-attribute-values).

| Property | Type | Values | Required for built-ins | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Id` | string | `^(?=.*[0-9.\-])[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]*([.\-][A-Za-z0-9_]+)*$`, max 64 | Yes | Never change an existing ID. |
| `Title` | string | One line | Yes | The only title. |
| `Product` | string | A product key from the taxonomy: `entra`, `exchange`, `defender`, ... | Yes | Write the key, not an alias such as `Entra ID`. Groups the console progress and the run summary. |
| `RelatedProduct` | string[] | Product keys | No | Never the same key as `Product`. `-Product` matches it too. |
| `Feature` | string | A feature key of the test's product: `conditional-access`, ... | Yes | |
| `Area` | string | An area key: `authentication`, `privileged-access`, ... | Yes | |
| `ResourceType` | string | A resource type key: `Tenant`, `User`, `ConditionalAccessPolicy`, ... | Yes | |
| `Severity` | string | `Critical`, `High`, `Medium`, `Low`, `Info` | Yes | A `TestSettings` row in a user's config overrides it. |
| `UserImpact` | string | `Low`, `Medium`, `High` | Yes, unless `Severity` is `Info` | Leave it out of an `Info` check. |
| `ImplementationCost` | string | `Low`, `Medium`, `High` | Yes, unless `Severity` is `Info` | Leave it out of an `Info` check. |
| `Mitre` | string[] | ATT&CK technique IDs (`T1110`, `T1110.003`), or the single value `None` | Yes | At most five. Never a technique beside one of its own sub-techniques. |
| `Control` | string[] | `<framework-key>:<requirement-id>` | CIS, CISA and ASD checks | The requirements the check implements or supports. A CIS check sets `Control = 'cis-m365:5.1.5.1'`, a CISA check `Control = 'cisa-scuba:MS.AAD.3.1'`, an ASD check `Control = 'essential-eight:ISM-1504'`; any other check may name the same requirements. The first one that a framework file knows becomes the `Benchmark` of the result. For a shipped framework the requirement must exist in its file. |
| `Service` | string[] | `Graph`, `Azure`, `ExchangeOnline`, `SecurityCompliance`, `SharePointOnline`, `Teams`, `Dataverse`, `AzureDevOps`, `GitHub`, `ActiveDirectory`, or `None` | Yes | All listed must be connected. Registry: `powershell/assets/MaesterServiceRegistry.psd1`. |
| `License` | string[] | Tokens from `powershell/assets/MaesterLicenseTable.psd1`; `A&B` = both | No | Tenant needs any one element. |
| `Permission` | string[] | `<Service>:<Kind>:<Name>`; `\|` joins alternatives | No | The permissions the check needs, for example `'Graph:Scope:Policy.Read.All'`. Every element is needed; inside an element any one alternative is enough, least privileged first. The service must be in `Service`, the kind one the service registry lists for it. Recorded; not enforced in 3.0. See "Permission" in `website/docs/writing-tests/index.mdx`. |
| `TenantType` | string[] | `Workforce`, `External` | No | Default `Workforce`. Recorded; enforced only when a run turns it on. |
| `Cloud` | string[] | `Commercial`, `GCC`, `GCCHigh`, `DoD`, `China`, `Bleu`, `Delos`, `GovSG` | No | Default all. Recorded; enforced only when a run turns it on. |
| `Platform` | string[] | `Windows`, `Linux`, `MacOS` | No | Declare `Windows` for Windows-only commands (lint checks common ones). |
| `Lifecycle` | string | `Preview`, `Stable`, `Deprecated` | No | Default `Stable`. Use `Preview` for a check that depends on preview APIs or is still being validated; it is not run by default. A `Deprecated` check still runs. |
| `ReplacedBy` | string | The ID of an existing test | No | Only with `Lifecycle = 'Deprecated'`. |
| `LongRunning` | bool | | No | Slow in large tenants. Not run by default. |
| `InstanceSource` | string | Function in the same file | No | Makes the check a family (below). |
| `Exclusive` | bool | | No | Must not run concurrently (for example it writes to the tenant). |
| `Tag` | string[] | No commas | No | Built-in checks do not use it. See [Tags](#tags). |
| `Author` | string[] | GitHub handles | Yes | The initial author(s). |
| `Contributor` | string[] | GitHub handles | No | Add yourself when you substantially change a check. |
| `HelpUrl` | string | `https://...` | No | Defaults to `https://maester.dev/docs/tests/<Id>`. |

`Category` and `Preview` were removed in 3.0. A test that still has one is `InvalidMetadata`, with the replacement
in the message: `Product` and `Feature` instead of `Category`, `Lifecycle = 'Preview'` instead of `Preview`.
Reserved names (rejected today): `OptionalService`, `TimeoutSeconds`.

Licence tokens: `AAD_PREMIUM` (Entra ID P1 or better), `AAD_PREMIUM_P2`, `Entra_Identity_Governance`,
`AAD_WRKLDID_P1`, `AAD_WRKLDID_P2`, `ATP_ENTERPRISE` (MDO P1 or P2), `THREAT_INTELLIGENCE` (MDO P2),
`EOP_ENTERPRISE`, `EXCHANGE_S_STANDARD`, `EXCHANGE_DLP`, `M365_ADVANCED_AUDITING`, `DEFENDER_XDR`,
`LOCKBOX_ENTERPRISE`, `INTUNE_A`. Built-in checks use only these; add a token to the table if you need a new one.

### Return values and outcomes

| The check does | Result | ReasonCode |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `return $true` / `return $false` | Passed / Failed | |
| `Add-MtTestResultDetail -Investigate` | Investigate (whatever it returns) | |
| `Add-MtTestResultDetail -SkippedBecause <code>` | Skipped; **the call ends the test** | `TestSkipped`, or `NotApplicable` |
| throws, or `-SkippedBecause Error` | Error | `TestError` |
| returns `$null` without skipping | Skipped | `NoResult` |
| returns a non-boolean or several values | Error | `InvalidReturn` |

- Return exactly one boolean. Uncaptured output (`$list.Add($x)`, a stray expression) becomes a second return value
  and an `InvalidReturn` error; send it to `$null` or `Out-Null`.
- The engine owns the `try`: any terminating or statement-terminating error ends the check as `Error` with the
  message. A `try`/`catch` is fine for a **specific** condition (for example a 403 reported as
  `-SkippedBecause NotAuthorized`), not as a blanket wrapper. A skip raised inside your own `try` still skips.
- Use `-SkippedBecause NotApplicable` when the tenant state makes the check meaningless (for example no policies of
  that kind exist). Never return `$null` to mean "not applicable".
- Never use `NotConnected*` or `NotLicensed*` skip codes in a built-in check; declare `Service` /
  `License`.
- Checks that need delegated permissions skip with `-SkippedBecause NotSupportedAppPermission` when
  `(Get-MgContext).AuthType -ne 'Delegated'`.

### Parameters

Tunable values are function parameters, never hard-coded and never read from wrapper arguments.

```powershell
param(
    # Longest validity period, in days, that a certificate may be issued for.
    [ValidateRange(1, 3650)]
    [int] $MaximumValidityDays = 365,

    # Members of these groups are exempt from this check.
    [MaesterParameter(Kind = 'Entra.Group')]
    [string[]] $ExcludedGroups
)
```

- Types: `int`, `bool`, `switch`, `string`, `string[]`. Constant defaults. Nothing mandatory: the check must run
  with no config.
- Every parameter has a **one-line** `#` comment directly above it (only the nearest comment line is read), or
  `.PARAMETER` help. The unit tests require a description.
- Thresholds get `ValidateRange`; choices get `ValidateSet`.
- `[MaesterParameter(Kind = ...)]` for IDs: `Entra.User`, `Entra.Group`, `Entra.ServicePrincipal`,
  `Entra.Application`, `Entra.ConditionalAccessPolicy`, `Entra.NamedLocation`, `Entra.Domain`,
  `Entra.DirectoryRole`, `Azure.Subscription`, `Azure.ResourceGroup`, `Azure.Resource`
  (`powershell/assets/MaesterParameterKinds.psd1`).
- `Instance` and names starting with `Mt` are engine-owned.
- Users set values in `maester-config.json` under `TestSettings[].Parameters`, or with
  `Invoke-MtTest -Parameter`.

### Families (one check, several results)

When a check produces one result per item, declare `InstanceSource = '<function in the same file>'`. The engine
calls that function at run time (never at discovery) and runs the check once per returned object, passed as
`$Instance` (declare `param($Instance)` with a description comment).

Each instance object has `Id` (required, unique, `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,127}$`; the row ID becomes
`<Id>.<suffix>`) and optional `Title`, `Severity`, `Tag`, `Data`. See `tests/maester/drift/Test.MT.1060.ps1` and
`tests/maester/entra/Test.MT.1024.ps1`.

### Settings

Read tenant-wide settings with `Get-MtSetting -Name <name>` (for example `EmergencyAccessAccounts`). New settings
Maester itself reads go in `powershell/assets/MaesterSettings.psd1` with a type, default and description.

## Data Retrieval

**Always prefer `Invoke-MtGraphRequest` over `Invoke-MgGraphRequest` or `Get-Mg*` cmdlets.** It provides:

- **Built-in caching** -- reduces API calls when multiple checks query the same endpoint.
- **Automatic pagination** -- no need for `-All`.
- **ConsistencyLevel header** -- included by default for read-only calls.
- **Batching** -- pass an array of IDs via `-UniqueId`.
- **Named parameters** -- `Select`, `Filter`, `QueryParameters`.

```powershell
$policies = Invoke-MtGraphRequest -RelativeUri 'policies/authorizationPolicy' -ApiVersion v1.0
$users = Invoke-MtGraphRequest -RelativeUri 'users' -Filter "userType eq 'Member'" -Select id, displayName
$users = Invoke-MtGraphRequest -RelativeUri 'users' -UniqueId $userIds -Select id, displayName, onPremisesSyncEnabled

$policySplat = @{
    ApiVersion      = 'beta'
    RelativeUri     = 'policies/roleManagementPolicyAssignments'
    Filter          = "scopeId eq '/' and scopeType eq 'DirectoryRole' and roleDefinitionId eq '$($role.id)'"
    QueryParameters = @{ expand = 'policy(expand=rules)' }
}
$policy = Invoke-MtGraphRequest @policySplat
```

Other helpers: `Get-MtConditionalAccessPolicy`, `Get-MtUser`, `Get-MtRole`, `Get-MtRoleMember`, `Get-MtGroupMember`,
`Get-MtExo`, `Get-MtSpo`, `Invoke-MtAzureRequest`, `Invoke-MtAzureResourceGraphRequest`. Caches are reached only
through these helpers; never assign `$script:`, `$global:` or `$__MtSession` state in a check (lint).

New Graph permission scopes go in `Get-MtGraphScope`.

## Result Formatting

```powershell
# Result text; the .md supplies the description
Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result $resultMarkdown

# Objects rendered as a table with admin portal deep links; -Result must contain %TestResult%
Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result "Found issues:`n`n%TestResult%" -GraphObjects $failing -GraphObjectType ConditionalAccess

# Needs a human to review
Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result $result -Investigate

# Custom skip
Add-MtTestResultDetail -SkippedBecause Custom -SkippedCustomReason 'All alerts have been suppressed.'
```

`-GraphObjectType`: `Users`, `Groups`, `Devices`, `ConditionalAccess`, `AuthenticationMethod`,
`AuthorizationPolicy`, `ConsentPolicy`, `Domains`, `IdentityProtection`, `UserRole`.

Output messages: a pass message starts with "Well done." and describes the positive outcome; a fail message says
what is wrong and what to change; tables have header and separator rows; link to the admin portal where possible.

## The Markdown File (`Test.<ID>.md`)

No front matter. Template:

```markdown
{One-line summary of what the check verifies.}

{Rationale: explain WHY this configuration matters for security.}

#### Remediation action

1. In **Entra ID**, navigate to **{Section}** > **[{Page Name}]({direct admin portal URL})**.
2. {Step-by-step instructions to fix the issue.}
3. Click **Save**.

#### Related links

* [{Admin portal link description}]({URL})
* [{Benchmark or baseline reference}]({URL})

<!--- Results --->
%TestResult%
```

- Exactly one `<!--- Results --->` followed by `%TestResult%`; everything above it is the description.
- Do not pass `-Description` to `Add-MtTestResultDetail`, so the `.md` is used.
- The `.md` is also shown for rows that did not run (not selected, service not connected), so it must make sense on
  its own.
- The website page `website/docs/tests/<suite>/<ID>.md` is generated from this file and the attribute.

## Choosing the Attribute Values

A built-in check says what it is about, how urgent a failure is and which attack techniques it addresses. Each
of those values is chosen with the [attribute rubric](../../../website/docs/writing-tests/attribute-rubric.md).
Read the rubric's section for an attribute before you set, change or review its value, and do not take the
values of a neighbouring check without checking them against it.

| Attribute | The question it answers |
| --- | --- |
| `Product` | In which product is the fix made? |
| `RelatedProduct` | Under which other products would an admin expect to find the check? Optional. |
| `Feature` | Which part of the product, a settings page or an object type, is the check about? |
| `Area` | Which security theme is it, whatever the product? |
| `ResourceType` | What does a failing result point at: the tenant, or a kind of object it lists? |
| `Severity` | How much risk does the organization carry while the check fails? |
| `UserImpact` | How much does the recommended fix disrupt end users? |
| `ImplementationCost` | How much administrator work does the recommended fix take? |
| `Mitre` | Which MITRE ATT&CK techniques does the checked control prevent or detect? |
| `Control` | Which requirements of CIS, CISA SCuBA, ASD Essential Eight, the ISM or NIST SP 800-53 does a passing result support? |

The rubric rates a check by the fix its own `.md` recommends, so write the `.md` before you choose the values.
The values of the generated EIDSCA and ORCA checks are in `build/eidsca/eidsca-test-metadata.json` and
`build/orca/orca-test-metadata.json`: change a value there and regenerate. The severity of an EIDSCA check is the
exception: it comes from the EIDSCA config upstream, so a change to it goes to the EIDSCA repository.

### Framework requirements and NIST controls (`Control`)

Fill in `Control` on every new check. Do not leave it out because it is optional: decide, and leave it empty
only when nothing applies. It is the only way a check is mapped to a framework. Work through these in order:

1. **The requirement the check is written for.** A CIS check lists `cis-m365:<id>` or `cis-github:<id>`, a
   CISA check lists `cisa-scuba:<id>` and an ASD check `essential-eight:<ISM id>` (or `ism:<ISM id>`), first. If the requirement is not in the suite's framework file yet, add it
   there with its facts (level and profiles, or criticality) in the same pull request.
2. **A CIS, CISA or ASD requirement that asks for the same setting.** A Maester check that verifies what
   `cisa-scuba:MS.AAD.3.1` asks for lists it. A benchmark check never adds its requirement to another suite's
   test: when that test already checks what the benchmark asks, the benchmark check is a shim (next section). Look the requirement up in `tests/cis/frameworks/*.json`,
   `tests/cisa/frameworks/cisa-scuba.json` and `tests/asd/frameworks/*.json`, or in the lookup of the [test builder](https://maester.dev/test-builder).
   `Get-MtTest -Suite CISA | Format-Table Id, Title, Control` shows what the existing checks map to.
3. **NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 controls**, written `nist-800-53-r5:<control>`, chosen with the NIST part of the
   rubric's [Control section](../../../website/docs/writing-tests/attribute-rubric.md#control) from the pinned list
   `powershell/assets/MaesterNistControls.json`. At most three, best fit first, and only when a passing result is
   direct evidence for the control. Skip this step when step 1 or 2 gave a `cisa-scuba` reference: CISA publishes
   the NIST mapping of its policies and the result gets it from the framework file.

The first value that names a requirement in a framework file becomes the `Benchmark` of the result, so the order
matters. An inventory count, or a health, licensing or tidiness check, usually lists nothing.

### A requirement another suite already checks (shims)

Benchmarks overlap: CIS, CISA, ASD and Maester tests often read the same setting. Before writing a check for a
benchmark requirement, and when reviewing one:

1. **Find the tests in every suite that read the setting.** `Get-MtTest -Product <key> -Feature <key> |
   Format-Table Id, Title`, and search `tests/` for the Graph endpoint or setting name.
2. **Read the benchmark's own sources**, not only the requirement's one-line text: its audit or assessment
   guidance and any reference configuration it publishes (CIS audit and remediation sections; the SCuBA baseline
   and ScubaGear; for ASD the ISM, the Essential Eight assessment process guide and the ASD Blueprint for Secure
   Cloud). Note every concrete value: a number of days, a threshold, a role list, an authentication strength, a
   rule that must be Block. Use the web tools; cite the page.
3. **Decide:**
   - Same check: write a **shim**, a test with its own `Id`, `Title`, `Control`, `Author` and `.md` whose body is
     `return <the other test's function>` (`return Test-MtCisMfaForEveryUser`).
   - Same check, different value that the other test takes as a parameter: a shim with its own parameter whose
     default is the benchmark's value, passed on (`return Test-MtCisSmartLockoutThreshold -MaximumLockoutThreshold $MaximumLockoutThreshold`).
   - Something no test checks, or a rule no parameter covers: a check of its own. Read data through
     `internal/services/<service>/` helpers, and move a helper there (with a neutral name) when another suite
     already has the code; never copy another check's logic or name a generic helper after a suite.

A shim declares the same `Product`, `RelatedProduct`, `Feature`, `Area`, `ResourceType`, `Severity`,
`UserImpact`, `ImplementationCost`, `Mitre`, `Service`, `License`, `Permission`, `TenantType`, `Cloud`,
`Platform`, `Lifecycle`, `LongRunning` and `Exclusive` as the test it calls; calls a test that is not a shim;
passes only parameters that test declares; leaves its own requirement off that test's `Control`; and says in its
`.md` what the benchmark asks and which test it runs, by ID. `powershell/tests/general/TestShims.Tests.ps1`
enforces all of this. The full guidance, with an example, is
[Tests that another suite already has](../../../website/docs/writing-tests/index.mdx#tests-that-another-suite-already-has).

When reviewing, fail a benchmark check that re-implements a check another suite already has when the benchmark's
sources give no reason for the difference, and say which test it duplicates and which source you read.

### Where the keys come from

- `Product`, `Feature`, `Area` and `ResourceType` take keys from `powershell/assets/MaesterTaxonomy.psd1`: the
  products with their features, the areas and the resource types. A feature key belongs to one product.
- `Product` follows the folder: a check in `tests/maester/entra` or `tests/cisa/entra` is `entra`. The folder map
  is in `powershell/tests/general/NativeTestLint.Tests.ps1`; a new service folder needs an entry there.
- `Mitre` takes technique IDs from the pinned ATT&CK release, `powershell/assets/MaesterAttackTechniques.json`.
  An ID that the release retired or does not know fails the unit tests. Tactics are looked up from the ID and
  never typed.
- `Control` takes requirement IDs from the framework files (`tests/<suite>/frameworks/<key>.json`) and NIST
  control IDs from `powershell/assets/MaesterNistControls.json`. The unit tests fail on an ID that is in neither.
- `Get-MtTest -Product entra -Feature conditional-access | Format-Table Id, Title, Severity, Area, ResourceType`
  lists the existing checks of a feature, to compare your values with.
- **A new key is added to the taxonomy in the same pull request as the first test that uses it.** Prefer an
  existing key. Do not add a key ahead of its test: the unit tests fail on a product, feature, area or resource
  type that no test uses. A new area also needs a row in the rubric's area table, which the unit tests compare
  with the taxonomy.

### Tags

`Tag` holds free labels for the owner of a test folder. It is not how Maester classifies a check.

- Built-in checks carry no tag for product, feature, area, suite, benchmark, licence, severity or their own ID.
  Each of those has an attribute or is derived, and the unit tests fail a built-in check that tags one. Remove
  such a tag when you edit an older check.
- Do not put `Preview` or `LongRunning` in `Tag`; use `Lifecycle = 'Preview'` and the `LongRunning` flag.
- Users select checks with `-Product`, `-Feature`, `-Area`, `-Severity` and `-Suite` on `Invoke-Maester` and
  `Get-MtTest`. The tags of Maester 2.x, such as `CA` or `CIS`, still select the checks that carried them, with a
  warning, through `powershell/assets/Maester.LegacyTags.json`. That file is generated and never edited, and a
  check added after 3.0 is not in it, so do not add a tag to make a new check selectable.
- A user's custom test may tag freely.

### How the values are checked

The unit tests in `powershell/tests/general/NativeTestAttributes.Tests.ps1` check what is mechanical. The
`attribute-review` check on the pull request has a reviewer model judge each new or changed value against the
rubric. The person or agent who reviews the pull request applies the same rubric. See
[How the rubric is enforced](../../../website/docs/writing-tests/attribute-rubric.md#how-the-rubric-is-enforced).

When the attribute review fails, change the value, or explain in the pull request why the declared value fits
the rubric. When you review a check yourself, follow "Reviewing a test's attributes" in
[AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md); it also shows how to run the attribute review before you push.

## Step-by-Step Workflow: Creating a New Check

1. **Look for a test that already checks it**, in every suite, and for a benchmark requirement read the
   benchmark's own sources. If the benchmark asks for what an existing test checks, the new check is a shim; see
   [A requirement another suite already checks](#a-requirement-another-suite-already-checks-shims).
2. **Reserve an ID.** Check [issue #697](https://github.com/maester365/maester/issues/697) and comment to reserve
   the next `MT.xxxx` (the maester-issue-manager agent can do this). `Get-MtTest MT.12*` shows which IDs exist.
3. **Scaffold** with `New-MtTest -Id <ID> -Title '...' -Service <service> -Product <product key>
   -Path ./tests/<suite>/<service>`.
4. **Fill in the attribute**: `License`, `Author`, flags as needed.
5. **Write the function**: read with `Invoke-MtGraphRequest` or the helpers, decide, `Add-MtTestResultDetail`,
   return a boolean. Add parameters for tunable values.
6. **Write the guide, the `.md`**, in full: a one-line summary, why the setting matters, numbered remediation
   steps with a direct link to the admin portal page, related links (Microsoft Learn, and the benchmark when the
   check maps to one), and the results footer. Replace every placeholder that `New-MtTest` wrote; a check with
   scaffold text in its guide is not finished. Verify product facts and links with Microsoft Learn.
7. **Choose the attribute values** with the rubric: `Feature`, `Area`, `ResourceType`, `Severity`, `UserImpact`,
   `ImplementationCost`, `Mitre`, `Control`, and `RelatedProduct` when one applies. See
   [Choosing the attribute values](#choosing-the-attribute-values) and
   [Framework requirements and NIST controls](#framework-requirements-and-nist-controls-control). The
   [test builder](https://maester.dev/test-builder) shows the allowed values and the rubric for each attribute
   and writes the attribute; use it to check a value you are unsure of.
8. **Validate offline**: `Import-Module ./powershell/Maester.psd1 -Force; Get-MtTest <ID>` must show
   `IsValid = True` and no `Errors`. Name the ID and leave out `-Path`: `Get-MtTest -Path <file>` applies the
   rules of a custom test, so it does not report a missing attribute or a key that is not in the taxonomy.
9. **Run against a tenant**: `Connect-Maester; Invoke-MtTest -Path <file>` (or `Invoke-MtTest -Id <ID>`). Try
   `-Parameter @{...}` for each parameter. Check the row's `Result`, `ReasonCode`, `ResultDetail.TestResult`.
10. **Run the unit tests**: `./powershell/tests/pester.ps1`. `powershell/tests/general/NativeTestLint.Tests.ps1`
   and `powershell/tests/general/NativeTestAttributes.Tests.ps1` check every built-in test.

## Converting a User's Pester-format Test

Users' 2.x custom tests (`*.Tests.ps1`) still run when Pester 5.7.1+ is installed. To convert:

```powershell
Convert-MtTest -Path ./custom -WhatIf
Convert-MtTest -Path ./custom | Format-Table Id, Status, Notes
```

It writes `Test.<ID>.ps1` + `.md` per `It`, turns a `Test-MtConnection` guard into `Service`, removes a blanket
`-SkippedBecause Error` catch, and rewrites a trailing `| Should -Be $true` to `return`. The `Describe` name
becomes `Feature`, so the row's `Block` stays what it was. The Pester tags are kept in `Tag`, except that a
`Preview` tag becomes `Lifecycle = 'Preview'` and a `LongRunning` tag the `LongRunning` flag. Rows marked
`NeedsReview` have `TODO` comments; tests with names built at run time are `Skipped` and must be rewritten as
families. Once converted, delete the Pester file: the native test runs and the Pester test with the same ID no
longer does.

A user's custom native test lives in their `custom/` folder, uses their own ID prefix (not `MT.`, `CISA.`, `CIS.`,
`EIDSCA.`, `ORCA.`, `AD-`, `AZDO.`, `MT1060.`, or `MP.`, which is reserved for Maester Packs), needs a `.md`, and needs only `Id` and `Title` in its attribute.
It may set `Product`, `Feature`, `Area` and `ResourceType` to values of its own (a value that matches the taxonomy
is stored as the key), may tag freely and may use `Control`; the rubric applies to it only if its owner wants it
to. It can call only Maester's exported commands; to reuse a built-in check it calls `Invoke-MtTest -Id <ID>`.

## Validation Checklist

### Test logic
- [ ] Returns exactly one `$true`/`$false`; no stray pipeline output.
- [ ] No other suite already checks the same setting; or the benchmark's own sources were read and the check is
      a shim of that test, or differs from it for a reason those sources give.
- [ ] No `Test-MtConnection` guard, no `Get-MtLicenseInformation` check; `Service` and `License` declared instead.
- [ ] No blanket `try { } catch { Add-MtTestResultDetail -SkippedBecause Error ... }`.
- [ ] `-SkippedBecause NotApplicable` (not `$null`) when the check does not apply.
- [ ] Data retrieval uses `Invoke-MtGraphRequest` or Maester helpers.
- [ ] No hard-coded GUIDs, tenant IDs or names; tunables are described parameters.
- [ ] No writes to `$script:`, `$global:`, `$env:` or `$__MtSession`.
- [ ] `Platform = 'Windows'` if it uses Windows-only commands.

### Attribute and files
- [ ] `Test.<Id>.ps1` and `Test.<Id>.md` in the right suite folder; ID unique and not reused.
- [ ] `Id`, `Title`, `Product`, `Feature`, `Area`, `ResourceType`, `Severity`, `Mitre`, `Service`, `Author` set;
      values constant.
- [ ] `UserImpact` and `ImplementationCost` set, or both left out when `Severity` is `Info`.
- [ ] `Product`, `Feature`, `Area` and `ResourceType` are keys from `powershell/assets/MaesterTaxonomy.psd1`; a
      new key is added there in this pull request.
- [ ] Each of those values, and `RelatedProduct` if set, checked against its section of the
      [attribute rubric](../../../website/docs/writing-tests/attribute-rubric.md), with the reason visible in
      the description or the remediation text.
- [ ] No `Category` or `Preview`; no `Tag` for product, feature, area, suite, benchmark, licence,
      severity or the ID. `Lifecycle = 'Preview'` and the `LongRunning` flag where they apply.
- [ ] A CIS, CISA or ASD check sets `Control` to its requirement (`cis-m365:<id>`, `cis-github:<id>`, `cisa-scuba:<id>`,
      `essential-eight:<id>` or `ism:<id>`), first, and the requirement is in the suite's framework file.
- [ ] `Control` was considered for every check: a CIS or CISA requirement that asks for the same setting, and
      NIST SP 800-53 controls from `powershell/assets/MaesterNistControls.json` (none when a `cisa-scuba`
      reference already brings them). Left empty only when nothing applies.
- [ ] `[CmdletBinding()]` and `[OutputType([bool])]`; comment-based help inside the function.
- [ ] `Get-MtTest <ID>` (without `-Path`) reports no errors.

### Documentation
- [ ] `.md` has summary, rationale, `#### Remediation action` with portal links, and ends with `<!--- Results --->` + `%TestResult%`.
- [ ] No scaffold placeholder is left in the `.md` ("Describe what this test checks", "Explain how to fix"), and its links open the page they name.
- [ ] Pass message starts with "Well done."; fail message is actionable.

### Code style
- [ ] One True Brace Style; Pascal Case; full cmdlet names (no aliases); 4-space indentation.
- [ ] UTF-8 with BOM for `.ps1` files.

### Pre-pull request
- [ ] `./powershell/tests/pester.ps1` passes (PSScriptAnalyzer included).
- [ ] Ran against a tenant with `Invoke-MtTest`.
- [ ] Commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/).

## Common Mistakes

| Mistake | Why it matters | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Adding a `Test-MtConnection` guard or licence check | Duplicates the engine's gate; lint fails | Declare `Service` / `License` |
| Wrapping the body in `try`/`catch` that reports `-SkippedBecause Error` | Lint fails; the engine already does it | Remove it; catch only specific conditions |
| Returning `$null` for "not applicable" | Reported as `Skipped`/`NoResult` | `Add-MtTestResultDetail -SkippedBecause NotApplicable` |
| Uncaptured output (`$list.Add(...)`) | `Error`/`InvalidReturn` | `$null = $list.Add(...)` |
| Variables or `@()` in the attribute | `InvalidMetadata` | Constants and `('a', 'b')` lists only |
| `Category` or `Preview` in the attribute | `InvalidMetadata`; both were removed in 3.0 | `Product` and `Feature`; `Lifecycle = 'Preview'` |
| A `Tag` such as `'CA'`, `'Entra'` or `'Maester'` on a built-in check | Unit tests fail; tags are not the taxonomy | Use the attribute that says it; see [Tags](#tags) |
| A product alias (`'Entra ID'`) or a key that is not in the taxonomy | Unit tests fail | Use the key from `powershell/assets/MaesterTaxonomy.psd1`, or add the key in the same pull request |
| Re-implementing a check another suite already has | Two tests give two answers for one setting and drift apart with every benchmark update | A shim that returns the other test's result; see [shims](#a-requirement-another-suite-already-checks-shims) |
| A generic helper named after a suite (`Get-MtAsd*`) in `internal/checks/<suite>/` | Other suites copy it instead of reusing it | A neutral name in `internal/services/<service>/` |
| Copying `Severity`, `Area` or `Mitre` from a similar check | The value may not fit this check, and the attribute review fails a value that does not fit | Choose each value with the rubric |
| Validating a built-in check with `Get-MtTest -Path` only | It applies the rules of a custom test and reports no missing attribute | `Get-MtTest <ID>` |
| File name does not match `Id` | `InvalidMetadata` | Rename to `Test.<Id>.ps1` |
| Missing `[CmdletBinding()]` | `InvalidMetadata` | Add it before `param()` |
| Hard-coded thresholds or object IDs | Users cannot tune the check | Make them described parameters |
| Multi-line `#` comment above a parameter | Only the last line is read as its description | One-line comment or `.PARAMETER` |
| `Invoke-MgGraphRequest` / `Get-Mg*` | Bypasses caching | `Invoke-MtGraphRequest` |
| Using `-Severity` or `-TestTitle` on `Add-MtTestResultDetail` | Ignored for single-result checks | Set them in the attribute |
| Editing generated EIDSCA/ORCA files or `website/docs/tests/` | Overwritten | Change the generator or the test files |
| Adding the function to `FunctionsToExport` | Check functions are internal in 3.0 | Don't |
| Missing `%TestResult%` in `-Result` with `-GraphObjects` | The object table is not inserted | Include the placeholder |

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Likely cause | Resolution |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Error` / `InvalidMetadata` | Attribute or file rule broken | `Get-MtTest <ID>` lists each problem with its line (`Get-MtTest -Path <file>` for a custom test) |
| Attribute review fails on the pull request | A value does not fit the rubric | Change it to the expected value, or explain in the pull request why the declared value fits |
| `Error` / `InvalidReturn` | Non-boolean or multiple outputs | Capture stray output; return one boolean |
| `Error` / `InvalidConfiguration` | Bad parameter value in config or `-Parameter` | Check `Get-MtTest <ID>` parameters; fix the value |
| `Error` / `TestError` | Exception in the body (often a permission) | Read `ReasonDetail` / `ErrorRecord` |
| `Skipped` / `ServiceNotConnected` | Declared service not connected | `Connect-Maester -Service <service>` |
| `Skipped` / `LicenseNotFound` | Tenant lacks every `License` element | Expected; check the token |
| `Skipped` / `NoResult` | Returned `$null` | Return a boolean or skip explicitly |
| `NotRun` / `LongRunning` or `Preview` | Excluded by default | `-IncludeLongRunning` / `-IncludePreview`, or `Invoke-MtTest -Id` |
| `NotRun` / `OptInServiceNotConnected` | Active Directory check without AD connection | `Connect-Maester -Service ActiveDirectory` |
| Report shows no description | `.md` missing, misnamed, or `-Description` passed | Name it `Test.<ID>.md`; drop `-Description` |
| `%TestResult%` appears literally | Placeholder missing from `-Result` with `-GraphObjects` | Add it |
| 403 from Graph | Missing scope | Add it to `Get-MtGraphScope` |
